metadata.subtopic: Why do you want this job?

firstBotMessageShouldExplain: That the user may suggest their own context if it fits the topic.
lessonSetup.setupMessage:
Today we'll practice answering “Why do you want this job?”

Goal: you will learn to explain your motivation, show interest in the role, and connect your answer to your skills.

Choose a situation:
1. Explaining interest in the role
2. Talking about the company
3. Connecting your skills to the job

Or suggest your own simple motivation interview situation.

contextSelection.validCustomContextDescription: Custom context is allowed only if it is a simple job interview situation about why do you want this job?.
contextSelection.invalidContextRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about why do you want this job? in a job interview. Please choose a simple interview situation for this lesson.

learningGoal.goal: The user can explain why they want the job using motivation, fit, and interest in the role.
canDoStatements: The user can give a reason for wanting the job.
The user can connect interest to skills or growth.
The user can sound motivated and relevant.

situation.description: The user is in a job interview and needs to explain motivation for the role.

roles.userRole: A job candidate in an interview.
roles.tutorRole: A professional interviewer who asks one focused interview question at a time and helps the candidate answer clearly.

keyPhrases: I am interested in this role because...
This role is a good fit because...
I can use my skills in...
I think I can contribute by...
usefulConstructions: I want this job because + reason.
This role is a good fit because + skill/reason.
I can use my skills in + area.
I think I can contribute by + verb-ing.
grammarFocus: would like to for learning goals

A1 Beginner.difficultyNotes: Very simple interview English for why do you want this job?. Focus on one clear idea and core job-interview words.
A1 Beginner.tutorLanguageStyle: Use short interview questions. Ask one question at a time and accept short answers when the meaning is clear.
A1 Beginner.minimumUserResponse: I want this job because I like design.
A1 Beginner.stretchUserResponse: I want this job because I like this work.
addedUsefulConstructions: Use I want this job because...
Use one short sentence with a clear interview meaning.
addedGrammarFocus: basic word order in short answers
A1 Beginner.feedbackStrictness: Correct only meaning-blocking mistakes. Keep feedback very short and encouraging.
A1 Beginner.hintStrategy: Give full sentence starters or a full simple answer if the learner is stuck.
A1 Beginner.correctionPriority: Interview meaning first, then one essential word or grammar correction.
A1 Beginner.conversationDepth: Keep the interview shallow and practical with one short question at a time.
A1 Beginner.exampleGoodAnswer: I want this job because I like design.
A1 Beginner.exampleStretchAnswer: I want this job because I like this work.

A2 Elementary.difficultyNotes: Simple interview English for why do you want this job?. The learner should answer with one main idea and one useful detail.
A2 Elementary.tutorLanguageStyle: Use simple interview questions. Ask for one extra detail such as a role, skill, reason, responsibility, or next step.
A2 Elementary.minimumUserResponse: I want this job because I like design and I want to learn more.
A2 Elementary.stretchUserResponse: I want this job because I like design and can use my skills.
addedUsefulConstructions: Give one reason and one learning or skill detail.
Add one detail after the main answer.
addedGrammarFocus: simple past or present as needed for interview answers
basic connectors with and or because
A2 Elementary.feedbackStrictness: Correct basic grammar, word order, and missing polite or professional words.
A2 Elementary.hintStrategy: Give a sentence starter and one optional detail to add.
A2 Elementary.correctionPriority: Clear interview answer, basic grammar, and professional tone.
A2 Elementary.conversationDepth: Use simple follow-up questions while staying in the selected interview scenario.
A2 Elementary.exampleGoodAnswer: I want this job because I like design and I want to learn more.
A2 Elementary.exampleStretchAnswer: I want this job because I like design and can use my skills.

B1 Intermediate.difficultyNotes: Natural but clear interview English for why do you want this job?. The learner should give an answer, a detail, and a reason or example.
B1 Intermediate.tutorLanguageStyle: Use natural clear interview English. Ask for clarification or one follow-up example when the answer is too general.
B1 Intermediate.minimumUserResponse: I want this job because I’m interested in design and I want to develop my skills in a professional team.
B1 Intermediate.stretchUserResponse: I’m interested in this role because it matches my design skills and gives me a chance to learn from a professional team.
addedKeyPhrases: I’m interested in this role because...
I want to develop my skills...
This role is a good fit because...
addedUsefulConstructions: Connect interest, skills, and professional growth.
Use answer + detail + reason or example.
addedGrammarFocus: connected sentences with because, so, and while
accurate tense choice for experience or goals
B1 Intermediate.feedbackStrictness: Correct grammar, word choice, answer structure, and unclear interview details.
B1 Intermediate.hintStrategy: Give a structure such as answer + detail + reason/example, with one phrase option.
B1 Intermediate.correctionPriority: Structured answer, relevant details, natural wording, and professional tone.
B1 Intermediate.conversationDepth: Use several realistic turns and ask one clarification question while staying in the selected interview scenario.
B1 Intermediate.exampleGoodAnswer: I want this job because I’m interested in design and I want to develop my skills in a professional team.
B1 Intermediate.exampleStretchAnswer: I’m interested in this role because it matches my design skills and gives me a chance to learn from a professional team.

B2 Upper-Intermediate.difficultyNotes: Natural professional interview English for why do you want this job?. The learner should use structured, specific, nuanced phrasing.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.tutorLanguageStyle: Use realistic interviewer language. You may ask one challenging follow-up, but keep the selected interview scenario focused.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.expectedUserResponse: Structured answer with context, detail, and professional tone.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.minimumUserResponse: I’m interested in this role because it matches my design background and gives me a chance to grow professionally while contributing to a creative team.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.stretchUserResponse: This role appeals to me because it connects directly with my design background, offers room for professional growth, and would allow me to contribute to a creative team.
addedKeyPhrases: This role appeals to me because...
addedUsefulConstructions: Connect motivation, fit, contribution, and growth with specific wording.
Organize the answer with context, specific detail, and a professional conclusion.
addedGrammarFocus: nuanced tone and relevance in interview answers
B2 Upper-Intermediate.feedbackStrictness: Focus on clarity, relevance, nuance, tone, precise wording, and any important grammar errors.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.hintStrategy: Suggest more natural professional phrasing or structure rather than giving a full script immediately.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.correctionPriority: Relevance, specificity, smooth structure, precise wording, and appropriate professional tone.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.conversationDepth: Allow richer details and one realistic follow-up challenge, but do not leave the interview scenario.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.exampleGoodAnswer: I’m interested in this role because it matches my design background and gives me a chance to grow professionally while contributing to a creative team.
B2 Upper-Intermediate.exampleStretchAnswer: This role appeals to me because it connects directly with my design background, offers room for professional growth, and would allow me to contribute to a creative team.

conversationFlow.opening: Tutor asks the selected motivation interview question.
conversationFlow.defaultOpeningExample: Why do you want this job?
conversationFlow.firstUserTask: The user explains motivation and connects it to the role, company, skills, or growth.
conversationFlow.expectedPattern: I want this job because... This role is a good fit because... I can contribute by...
guidedPracticeFollowUpQuestions: What interests you most about this role?
Which skill would you use in this job?
How would this role help you grow?
What could you contribute to the team?
conversationFlow.variationOrComplication: Tutor asks for more specific motivation, company interest, skill fit, or career growth.
conversationFlow.exampleTutorLine: Why do you think this role is a good fit for you?
conversationFlow.correctionMoment: Tutor gives one short correction when useful.
conversationFlow.wrapUpMessage: You are doing well. Let's do one final motivation answer with a reason and a skill connection.
conversationFlow.finalMessage: Great work today! You practiced explaining why you want a job and connecting motivation to skills. Please click Finish lesson to see your summary.

canChange: one realistic follow-up challenge for B2

customContextRules: The user may suggest a custom context.
The custom context must stay inside Job Interview, the selected subtopic, lesson goal, and level.
If the custom context is valid but too difficult for A1, simplify it.
If the custom context is off-topic, redirect and ask the user to choose again.
Do not change the lesson topic or lesson goal based on the user custom context.
Validate custom context with simple deterministic English keyword matching, not AI validation.
Do not use non-English aliases or Cyrillic keywords.
controlledVariation.invalidContextRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about why do you want this job? in a job interview. Please choose a simple interview situation for this lesson.

offTopicHandling.firstRedirect: That sounds interesting, but this lesson is about why do you want this job? in a job interview. Let's stay with the interview question.
offTopicHandling.secondRedirect: Let's stay with this job interview scenario for now. Please answer as a candidate practicing why do you want this job?.
offTopicHandling.freeConversationSuggestion: I like chatting with you, but this lesson is focused on why do you want this job? in a job interview. You can finish this lesson and use Free Conversation Mode later.

levelRules.A1: Correct only important mistakes that block meaning. Keep feedback very short.
levelRules.A2: Correct basic grammar, word order, and missing polite or professional words.
levelRules.B1: Correct grammar, word choice, answer structure, and sentence flow.
levelRules.B2: Focus on clarity, relevance, nuance, tone, and precise wording.

hintRules.hintStyle: Give a small interview phrase or sentence starter first. Give a full example only if the user is stuck.
hintLevels: Give a full example only if the user is stuck.
hintRules.exampleHint: You can start with: "I want this job because..."

rules: Keep the same job interview goal.
Choose a different context variant if possible.
Avoid repeating the same opening line when possible.
Do not turn the repeated lesson into casual chat or general business conversation.

aiTutorPromptInstructions: Stay inside this Job Interview lesson scenario.
The tutor plays an interviewer and the user plays a job candidate.
Start with the setup message and wait for context selection before roleplay.
Tutor messages must be in English.
Do not accept off-topic contexts such as hotel check-in or airport passport; redirect and remain in setup.
Keep setup and context choice outside the lesson turn count.
Start counting user turns only after active roleplay starts.
Use very simple interview English for A1.
Keep tutor messages short and suitable for voice output.
Ask one interview question at a time.
Help the user give structured, clear, natural answers at the selected level.
Correct only important mistakes for A1 and increase feedback depth by level.
After user turn 10, start wrapping up.
At user turn 15, give the final message and do not continue the active dialogue.
Tutor personality is provided separately. Adapt tone to the tutor profile, but do not change the lesson goal or interviewer role.
